abstract: Maintains sensor ionization hardware records, scan frequencies, and linear saturation ceiling ratings
system_message:
You are Spectrometry instrumentation lead (SPEC). The Spectrometry instrumentation lead (SPEC) oversees sensor ionization hardware certifications, continuous spectral scan frequencies, and linear saturation ceiling ratings across contamination localization systems, ensuring instrument hardware configurations adhere to cleanroom diagnostic baselines.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Chassis electrical load（PWR）
information_points.content:
SPEC-PWR-CU5：Differential vacuum photoionization mass spectrometry exhibits a peak power draw of 700 W on the mobile diagnostic cart under continuous full-spectrum sampling.
SPEC-PWR-E2X：Proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight spectrometry registers a peak power draw of 500 W under continuous diagnostic cart operation.
SPEC-PWR-DVQ：The cavity ring-down spectroscopic point grid exhibits a peak power draw of 350 W during active mobile cart sampling.

information_points.title: Maintains sensor ionization hardware records, scan frequencies, and linear saturation ceiling ratings（ANL）
information_points.content:
SPEC-ANL-IDK：For proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight spectrometry, the sampling ionization module possesses cleanroom emission certification, the detector scan rate across the full mass spectrum is 75 Hz, and the linear saturation ceiling is 500 ppb.
SPEC-ANL-OVP：For differential vacuum photoionization mass spectrometry, the protocol sampling ionization chamber holds cleanroom emission certification, the detector scan frequency during continuous spectral acquisition across the targeted VOC mass range is 75 Hz, and the linear saturation ceiling on the calibration curve is 1250 ppb.
SPEC-ANL-XIV：For the cavity ring-down spectroscopic point grid, the protocol sampling ionization chamber is certified for cleanroom emissions, the continuous detector scan frequency across the target VOC mass range is 20 Hz, and the upper linear saturation ceiling reaches 1250 ppb.
